case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: The Court held that DHHR kept its statutory responsibility for filing the case plan even after a private agency was made case manager, that foster parents may participate in abuse and neglect proceedings in a limited way, and that a child has a right to continued contact with those with whom he has formed a close bond when that serves his best interests.
key_cases.relevance: It is the WV authority that the statutory case-plan duty is the Department's and is non-delegable to a private case manager.
key_cases.quote: we believe that DHHR nonetheless retained its statutory responsibility with regard to the filing of a case plan with the court under West Virginia Code § 49-6-5

key_cases.case_name: In the Interest of Carlita B.
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Affirming termination of parental rights, the Court held the improvement periods and family case plans afforded the mother were more than adequate, and directed that abuse and neglect cases be given the highest priority with systems developed to monitor their progress and prevent delay.
key_cases.relevance: It is the leading WV authority on the adequacy of court-ordered improvement periods and the family case plans that implement them.
key_cases.quote: Unjustified procedural delays wreak havoc on a child's development, stability and security.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Affirming denial of post-adjudicatory and dispositional improvement periods and the termination of parental rights, the Court held that an improvement period is a carefully limited, discretionary opportunity that must be denied where granting it would jeopardize the child's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: It is the WV standard governing whether court-ordered rehabilitative services (improvement periods) must be granted.
key_cases.quote: Where an improvement period would jeopardize the best interests of the child, for instance, an improvement period will not be granted

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Affirming termination of parental rights but reversing the summary denial of post-termination visitation, the Court held that the circuit court did not err in refusing to extend the improvement period or order long-term foster care where no evidence showed a reasonable likelihood of improvement.
key_cases.relevance: It is the controlling WV decision on court-ordered rehabilitative services — the family case plan that implements an improvement period, the permissible length of that period, and the parent's own statutory responsibility for initiating and completing its terms.
key_cases.quote: Given the lack of any evidence showing a reasonable likelihood of improvement, we find no error in the circuit court's refusal to extend the respondent's improvement period

key_cases.case_name: State ex rel. West Virginia Department of Human Services v. Cheryl M.
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Reversing termination of parental rights, the Court held that the mother was entitled to a meaningful improvement period absent compelling circumstances and that DHS failed to comply with W. Va. Code § 49-6D-3 by never preparing a court-approved family case plan or rendering good-faith assistance under it.
key_cases.relevance: It is the WV authority, relied on in Diva P. and discussed in Charity H., that a court-ordered improvement period must be accompanied by a court-approved family case plan supplying detailed, measurable standards against which improvement can be judged.
key_cases.quote: when an improvement period is authorized, then the court by order shall require the DHS to prepare a family case plan pursuant to W.Va.Code, 49-6D-3 (1984)

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of Appeals of West Virginia
key_cases.holding: Affirming termination of parental rights, the Court held that the trial court did not err in refusing an improvement period the mother first requested after the final hearing, and that sufficient evidence supported the finding of no reasonable likelihood that the conditions of neglect could be substantially corrected.
key_cases.relevance: It is the WV authority that the statutory entitlement to court-ordered rehabilitative services is forfeited unless the parent moves for an improvement period before the final hearing, and it applies the R.J.M. least-restrictive-alternative standard in affirming termination.
key_cases.quote: In view of this delay and of the failure to make a timely request, we find that the trial court did not err in refusing an improvement period.
